title: NIS2 cybersecurity (add-on)
description: NIS2 on the Core registers and the NIS2 requirement library: a scope self-check per legal entity (essential or important) with its registration, the ten Art. 21(2) measures as controls in the shared Controls library, incident reports with the 24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification and one-month final report and their clocks, and management body approval and training (Art. 20) through an approval workflow. A country setting lists every EU and EEA country with its authority, CSIRT, registration route and notes (unverified until checked) and fills them in as defaults. Installs the Core registers (Full: the Controls library and Competence and training) first when they are missing. Own words; article headings are the official ones.

settings.label: Country of main establishment
settings.description: The EU or EEA country whose NIS2 rules you follow first. It sets the default authority, CSIRT, registration route and national notes on new scope records and incident reports. Groups with entities in several countries can change the value on each record.

sheets.name: NIS2 scope and registration
sheets.description: A self-check per legal entity: is it in scope of NIS2 (Art. 2), essential or important (Art. 3), and is it registered with the authority (Art. 3(4), Art. 27)? The suggested class is worked out from the sector, the size and any rule that applies regardless of size; a person confirms it.

fields.name: Country of main establishment
fields.description: Set from the pack setting; change it for an entity established elsewhere.

fields.name: Annex
fields.description: Annex I sectors are of high criticality, Annex II sectors are other critical sectors.

config.expr: IF(OR({sector} = "Energy", {sector} = "Transport", {sector} = "Banking", {sector} = "Financial market infrastructure", {sector} = "Health", {sector} = "Drinking water", {sector} = "Waste water", {sector} = "Digital infrastructure", {sector} = "ICT service management (business to business)", {sector} = "Public administration", {sector} = "Space"), "Annex I", IF(OR({sector} = "Postal and courier services", {sector} = "Waste management", {sector} = "Chemicals", {sector} = "Food", {sector} = "Manufacturing", {sector} = "Digital providers", {sector} = "Research"), "Annex II", ""))

fields.name: Size
fields.description: Medium or larger: 50 or more staff, or both turnover and balance sheet above EUR 10 million. Large: 250 or more staff, or turnover above EUR 50 million and balance sheet above EUR 43 million. Count partner and linked enterprises as the SME rules say.

config.expr: IF(AND(EMPTY({employees}), EMPTY({turnover})), "", IF(OR({employees} >= 250, AND({turnover} > 50, {balance} > 43)), "Large", IF(OR({employees} >= 50, AND({turnover} > 10, {balance} > 10)), "Medium", "Small")))

fields.name: In scope whatever the size
fields.description: Rules that bring an entity in scope regardless of its size (Art. 2(2) to 2(4), Art. 3(1)).

options.label: Qualified trust service provider, TLD registry or DNS service provider
Public electronic communications network or service
Critical entity under the CER Directive

fields.name: Suggested class
fields.description: A first answer from the fields above, not a legal opinion. Confirm it in Classification.

config.expr: IF(AND(EMPTY({sector}), EMPTY({special_case})), "", IF(OR({special_case} = "Qualified trust service provider, TLD registry or DNS service provider", {special_case} = "Central government body", {special_case} = "Critical entity under the CER Directive"), "Essential", IF({special_case} = "Public electronic communications network or service", IF({size} = "Small", "Important", "Essential"), IF({special_case} = "Designated by the Member State", "Essential or important, as designated", IF(OR({special_case} = "Trust service provider (not qualified)", {special_case} = "Domain name registration services only"), IF(AND({size} = "Large", {annex} = "Annex I"), "Essential", "Important"), IF(AND({size} = "Large", {annex} = "Annex I"), "Essential", IF(AND(OR({size} = "Large", {size} = "Medium"), OR({annex} = "Annex I", {annex} = "Annex II")), "Important", "Probably not in scope")))))))

fields.name: Classification
fields.description: Confirmed by a person, with the reasoning below.

rules.message: Write why the entity is in this class and name an owner before confirming it.

fields.label: Which sector is its main activity in?
Subsector and type of entity (as the annexes name them)
Does any of these apply, whatever the size?

sheets.name: NIS2 incident reports
sheets.description: The reporting of a significant incident to the CSIRT or authority (Art. 23) in its stages: early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware, incident notification within 72 hours, final report within one month of the notification (a progress report first if the incident is still going on). The incident itself stays in the shared Incidents register.

fields.name: Became aware at
fields.description: When you became aware of the significant incident: the clocks run from here.

fields.name: Significant incident?
fields.description: Significant: it caused or can cause severe disruption of the services or financial loss for you, or considerable damage to others (Art. 23(3)). National rules and implementing acts may set thresholds.

rules.message: Record when the early warning and the notification went out and the final report before closing.
Write why the incident is not significant before closing it as not reportable.

fields.name: Report to
fields.description: The CSIRT or authority you report to. Set from the pack setting.

fields.name: Initial assessment
fields.description: Severity and impact, and the indicators of compromise where you have them.

fields.name: Final report due
fields.description: One month after the notification. If the incident is still going on then, send a progress report and the final report within a month of handling it.

fields.name: Final report
fields.description: A detailed description with the severity and impact, the type of threat or root cause, the mitigation applied and going on, and any cross-border impact.

fields.name: Reference from the CSIRT or authority
Service recipients told
fields.description: Where the incident is likely to affect the services you provide to them (Art. 23(1)).

items.name: Example: Ransomware on the route planning servers

values.significance_reasoning: Route planning down for 30 hours; deliveries in two countries late.
values.initial_assessment: High impact on deliveries; contained to the planning cluster; indicators shared with the CSIRT.

sheets.name: NIS2 management body decisions
sheets.description: What the management body approves and oversees (Art. 20): the cybersecurity risk-management measures, the yearly review of how they work, and its own training. Each decision goes through the approval workflow so who approved what, and when, is on record.

fields.name: Approval step
fields.description: Where the decision is in its approval. Set by the approval workflow, never by hand.

items.name: Example: Approve the cybersecurity risk-management measures for 2027

values.summary: The management body approves the ten baseline measures in the Controls library tagged NIS2, their owners and the budget, and asks for a review of how they work in twelve months.

items.name: Example: Cybersecurity training for the management body

values.summary: Every member of the management body completes the yearly cybersecurity training; staff are offered the same.

fields.name: NIS2 measure
fields.description: The Art. 21(2) measure this control puts in place.

items.name: Risk analysis and information system security policies (NIS2 21(2)(a))
Incident handling (NIS2 21(2)(b))
Business continuity, backups, disaster recovery and crisis management (NIS2 21(2)(c))
Supply chain security, including direct suppliers (NIS2 21(2)(d))
Security in buying, building and maintaining systems, with vulnerability handling and disclosure (NIS2 21(2)(e))
Checking whether the measures work (NIS2 21(2)(f))
Basic cyber hygiene and cybersecurity training (NIS2 21(2)(g))
Use of cryptography and encryption (NIS2 21(2)(h))
People security, access control and asset management (NIS2 21(2)(i))
Multi-factor sign-in, secured voice, video and text, and secured emergency communications (NIS2 21(2)(j))

items.name: Cybersecurity (NIS2)

values.likelihood_scale: 1 Rare: no known attempts against us or our sector. 2 Unlikely: attempts seen in our sector. 3 Possible: attempts seen against us. 4 Likely: expected within a year. 5 Almost certain: happening now.
values.impact_scale: 1 Negligible: no effect on the services. 2 Minor: a short slowdown, no customer notices. 3 Moderate: a service down for hours, some customers affected. 4 Major: services down for a day or more, or data lost; reportable. 5 Severe: long disruption with harm to customers or society, or large financial loss.

items.name: Example: Ransomware stops order handling for several days

values.cause: Phishing or an unpatched system gives an attacker a foothold
values.consequence: Orders and deliveries stop; a significant incident to report within 24 hours

automations.name: Incident significant → stage Early warning due
Early warning sent → stage Notification due
automations.description: Stages: recording when the early warning went out moves the report to "Notification due", so the board always shows the next deadline the reporting lead has to meet.

automations.name: Notification sent → stage Final report due
Early warning: 8 hours left → tell the lead and the security officer

actions.message: {id} {name}: 8 hours left to send the early warning to {recipient}. Send what you know now: whether it looks malicious and whether it could affect other countries.

automations.description: SLA clock: 16 hours after you became aware of a possibly significant incident, the reporting lead and the security officer are told that the 24-hour early warning is due in 8 hours.

automations.name: Early warning: 2 hours left → escalate to top management

actions.message: {id} {name}: the 24-hour early warning to {recipient} is due in 2 hours and has not been sent.

automations.description: Escalation ladder: with 2 hours left on the 24-hour clock, top management joins the reporting lead and the security officer, because the management body answers for reporting on time.

automations.name: Notification: 24 hours left → tell the lead and the security officer

actions.message: {id} {name}: the 72-hour incident notification to {recipient} is due in 24 hours. Update the early warning with an initial assessment: severity, impact and indicators of compromise.

automations.description: SLA clock: 48 hours after you became aware, the reporting lead and the security officer are reminded that the incident notification with the initial assessment is due within 24 hours.

automations.name: Final report due in 7 days → tell the lead

actions.message: {id} {name}: the final report to {recipient} is due on {final_due}. If the incident is still going on, send a progress report instead.

automations.name: Final report overdue → escalate to the security officer and top management

actions.message: {id} {name}: the final report was due on {final_due} and has not been sent to {recipient}.

automations.description: Escalation: a final report still missing the day after its one-month deadline goes to the reporting lead, the security officer and top management.

automations.name: Classification changes → ask the owner to update the registration within two weeks

actions.message: {id} {name} is now {classification}. Tell {authority} about the change within two weeks and record it here.

automations.description: Gate on the registration: when a registered entity’s classification changes, its owner is asked to tell the authority within two weeks (Art. 3(4)) and the request stays open in their My work until the record changes.

automations.name: Scope re-check in 30 days → ask the owner

actions.message: Re-check {id} {name} by {next_review}: staff, turnover, activities and national designations still as recorded?

automations.name: Decision approved → set the next review in a year
automations.description: Recurring review: when the management body approves a decision, the date is recorded and the next review is set a year ahead, so the measures are approved and overseen every year.

automations.name: Decision review in 30 days → ask who prepared it

actions.message: Prepare the yearly review of {id} {name} for the management body by {next_review}.

setup.title: NIS2 setup
setup.description: Six steps to show that NIS2 is in hand. Choose your country in the pack’s settings first (Workspace admin › Packs › NIS2 › Settings): it fills in the authority, CSIRT and registration route. Give the security lead the job title "Information security officer" and the management body "Top management".

steps.title: Check each entity is in scope
steps.body: Run the self-check for each legal entity in the group (the form does it), then confirm essential, important or not in scope with the reasoning.

steps.title: Register with the authority
steps.body: Each essential or important entity registers as the national law sets out. Record the date and the reference.

steps.title: Put the Art. 21 measures in place
steps.body: The ten measures are in the Controls library tagged NIS2. Give each an owner, test it and mark the NIS2 articles applicable with their status.

steps.title: Have the management body approve the measures
steps.body: Submit the decision to approve the measures. The security officer reviews it, then every member of the management body approves.

steps.title: Train the management body
steps.body: Record the decision on training and each member’s training in Competence and training, ticking "Management body member".

steps.title: Be ready to report within 24 hours
steps.body: Check "Report a cyber incident" on Incidents and the CSIRT on the reports sheet, name a reporting lead and rehearse the 24-hour, 72-hour and one-month stages once.
